_note: One fun fact per playable country for the passport book. Stable textbook facts, fact-checked by Forge (Oct 2026); chosen so none repeats the topic of a question about the same country.

facts.CAN: Canada has the longest coastline of any country in the world.
facts.USA: The USA has 50 states: Alaska is the biggest and Rhode Island the smallest.
facts.MEX: People in what is now Mexico were making chocolate drinks from cacao beans more than 3,000 years ago.
facts.GTM: More than 20 Mayan languages are still spoken in Guatemala today.
facts.CUB: Cuba is home to the bee hummingbird, the smallest bird in the world.
facts.PAN: Panama hats aren't from Panama! They're woven in Ecuador, but became famous when canal workers wore them.
facts.CRI: Costa Rica has had no army since 1948 and spends the money on schools and health instead.
facts.JAM: Jamaica sent a bobsleigh team to the 1988 Winter Olympics in Canada, even though Jamaica has no snow.
facts.DOM: Larimar, a sky-blue gemstone, is found only in the Dominican Republic.
facts.HTI: Haiti is famous for its painters, whose bright, colourful pictures of everyday life are sold all over the world.
facts.HND: The scarlet macaw, a big red, yellow and blue parrot, is the national bird of Honduras.
facts.SLV: El Salvador is the only Central American country with no Caribbean coastline. Its only coast is on the Pacific.
facts.BRA: Brazil borders every country in South America except Chile and Ecuador.
facts.ARG: Argentina is the eighth-largest country in the world.
facts.CHL: Chile is more than 4,000 km long but never more than about 350 km wide.
facts.PER: Potatoes were first grown in the Andes of Peru and Bolivia thousands of years ago, and Peru still has thousands of kinds.
facts.COL: Colombia is the only South American country with coasts on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.
facts.VEN: Venezuela has the largest known oil reserves of any country in the world.
facts.ECU: Ecuador uses the US dollar as its money.
facts.BOL: La Paz in Bolivia uses cable cars as everyday public transport, gliding over the city high in the Andes.
facts.PRY: Paraguay's flag has a different picture in the middle on each side, front and back.
facts.URY: Uruguay was the first country to give a free laptop to every child in its state primary schools.
facts.GUY: St George's Cathedral in Georgetown, Guyana, is one of the tallest wooden churches in the world.
facts.SUR: Suriname is the smallest country in South America, and rainforest covers most of it.
facts.GBR: The United Kingdom is made of four countries: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
facts.IRL: Ireland's national symbol is the harp, which appears on Irish euro coins.
facts.FRA: Thanks to its overseas territories around the world, France has more time zones than any other country.
facts.ESP: Spain's national anthem has no official words, so people hum or sing 'la la la' along to it.
facts.PRT: Portugal and England signed a friendship treaty in 1373. It's the oldest alliance in the world that is still in force.
facts.DEU: Johannes Gutenberg built his famous printing press with movable type in Mainz, Germany, around 1450.
facts.ITA: Many music words, like piano, forte and allegro, come from Italian.
facts.NLD: There are more bicycles than people in the Netherlands.
facts.POL: In Poland's Wieliczka Salt Mine, miners carved whole chapels, statues and chandeliers out of salt.
facts.SWE: Sweden's Icehotel is built again from ice and snow every winter, then melts back into the river in spring.
facts.NOR: In northern Norway the sun doesn't set for weeks in summer. This is called the midnight sun.
facts.GRC: Greece has about 6,000 islands, but only around 200 of them have people living on them.
facts.EGY: Ancient Egyptians wrote on papyrus, a kind of paper made from reeds that grow along the Nile.
facts.MAR: Chefchaouen, a town in Morocco's mountains, is famous for its streets and houses painted in shades of blue.
facts.NGA: More than 500 languages are spoken in Nigeria.
facts.KEN: Kenyan runners have won many Olympic gold medals in long-distance races.
facts.ZAF: South Africa's Kruger National Park is home to the 'Big Five': lions, leopards, elephants, rhinos and buffalo.
facts.ETH: Ethiopia has its own calendar with 13 months, so its new year falls in September.
facts.GHA: In Ghana's Kakum National Park, a canopy walkway of rope bridges lets you walk high up in the rainforest treetops.
facts.DZA: Algeria's capital, Algiers, is nicknamed 'Algiers the White' because of its bright white buildings.
facts.TUN: The northernmost point of the whole African continent is in Tunisia.
facts.TZA: Jane Goodall began her famous study of wild chimpanzees at Gombe Stream in Tanzania in 1960.
facts.SEN: The baobab tree, which stores water in its huge trunk, is a national symbol of Senegal.
facts.MDG: Madagascar is the fourth-largest island in the world.
facts.CHN: China is about as wide as the USA, yet the whole country uses just one time zone.
facts.IND: Chess grew out of chaturanga, a game first played in India about 1,500 years ago.
facts.JPN: Sumo wrestling is Japan's national sport, and it has been around for more than 1,000 years.
facts.KOR: The Korean alphabet, Hangul, was invented in the 1440s under King Sejong so everyone could learn to read.
facts.IDN: Indonesia's rainforests are home to orangutans, whose name means 'person of the forest' in Malay.
facts.THA: Thailand is the only country in Southeast Asia that was never ruled by a European power.
facts.VNM: Vietnam grows more coffee than any country except Brazil.
facts.PHL: The Philippine eagle is one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
facts.MYS: Malaysia's rainforests are home to the rafflesia, a flower that can grow almost a metre wide.
facts.SAU: Saudi Arabia has no permanent rivers at all.
facts.TUR: Istanbul sits on two continents, Europe and Asia, divided by the Bosporus strait.
facts.PAK: The Khewra Salt Mine in Pakistan is one of the oldest and largest salt mines in the world.
facts.BGD: Bangladesh is one of the most densely populated countries in the world.
facts.MNG: Mongolia has fewer people per square kilometre than any other country in the world.
facts.AUS: Anna Creek, a cattle farm in Australia, is the biggest in the world. It's larger than some whole countries!
facts.NZL: In 1893 New Zealand became the first country where women could vote in national elections.
facts.PNG: Papua New Guinea shares New Guinea, the world's second-largest island, with Indonesia.
facts.FJI: Fijians greet each other with a big, friendly 'Bula!'
facts.VUT: On Vanuatu's Pentecost Island, land divers leap from tall wooden towers with vines tied to their ankles. It's the idea behind bungee jumping.
facts.SLB: The Solomon Islands' Marovo Lagoon is one of the largest saltwater lagoons in the world.
